column1: # Hostile inputs for the triage task (Slice 5 of docs/plans/hyalos-kernel-python, S-06.1).
# Each `#` line is a comment, and the comment before a case names what it tries. Every other line
# is `<case id>\t<runtime or all>\t<data line>`; a case's data file is its lines in order. In the
# data line `\xNN` is the byte NN, a backslash is always written `\x5c` and a tab `\x09`, and
# any other character is itself. spikes/438/hostile.sh decodes each case into
# spikes/438/evidence/data/<runtime>-hostile-<case id>.tsv and runs it at seed 0, where the stub
# model labels a title by its words alone (`hyalos-os/monitor/src/main.rs`, `stub_model`): a title
# that says "security" is labelled security and so is copied into the notification.
# utf8: titles that are not UTF-8 (S-06.1.e1): invalid start bytes, an overlong NUL, a lone
# surrogate and a sequence cut short. Each says "security", so each is copied into the notification.
# record-16384: a record of exactly 16,384 bytes, the guest's read buffer (S-06.1.e2), then one
# ordinary record. Its title is longer than the 4,096 bytes the script asks about.
# record-16385: a record of 16,385 bytes, one more than the read buffer (S-06.1.e2), then one
# ordinary record. The guest reads it as too large, which the SDK counts as other without asking.
# numbers: issue numbers the SDK's own parser must refuse: over 2^32 - 1, signed, spaced, empty,
# hexadecimal and not ASCII digits. Each title says "security", so a number it took would be
# repr: titles aimed at the Monty guest's reading of a bytes value back from its repr
# (spikes/438/monty/guest/src/lib.rs, `bytes_of`): both quotes, backslashes, a literal \x41 and
# \n, a tab, a carriage return that draws a forged line on a terminal, a NUL and high bytes, and
# a title that is itself a bytes literal. Each says "security", so each crosses the guest boundary
# twice, in the question and in the notification. MicroPython runs it as a control.
